claims.statement: Polish health authorities define laboratory diagnostics as regulated testing of patient material with quality requirements, making each authorized test an identifiable fulfillment event; public sources cited do not establish marketplace pricing or unused capacity.
The proposed payer is a clinic operations function or participating laboratory commercial function at order fulfillment; willingness to pay a separate routing fee is unverified.
Control can only be obtained through signed laboratory capacity and processing agreements; there is no current special access, and the founder must not perform or interpret regulated diagnostic work.
Health data receives special GDPR protection, so a routing layer should minimize identifiable results and establish a valid role and legal basis rather than rely on generic consent language.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Clinic operations lead or laboratory commercial director
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: True multi-lab resilience, standardized panels, and clinic-owned patient experience must beat a single chain's integrated portal
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Clinic retains the patient relationship; founder company owns its B2B clinic and laboratory contracts
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Direct B2B clinic outreach and multiple nonexclusive licensed-lab supply contracts

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Founder-led clinic sales and lab business-development cycles; target below six months of gross profit
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Clinic prepayment or short invoice terms; avoid funding laboratory receivables during the pilot
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unknown; target 15-25% transaction margin plus high-margin software fees after support
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Panel mapping, integration, consent workflow, rejection handling, and B2B service desk
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Health-law counsel, GDPR controls, DPIA where required, security, insurance, and vendor qualification
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 500-1500 PLN monthly clinic fee plus 5-10% contracted take rate on fulfilled panels
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Laboratory charges if merchant-of-record, collection fees, messaging, payments, and order support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Large laboratory chains can bundle ordering portals, collection networks, pricing, and results
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Each clinician-authorized laboratory test order is a discrete fulfillment event; rejected specimens, duplicate coordination, and excess turnaround are measurable operating losses
commercial_mechanics.payer: Private clinic or contracted laboratory, never the founder acting as a medical provider
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Growing panel volume, multi-city collection needs, turnaround failures, or manual invoice reconciliation
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each fulfilled order plus clinic and lab agreement renewal

contrary_evidence: Large laboratory networks already provide collection, ordering, and results portals.
Polish laboratory medicine is tightly regulated, reducing the founder's allowable operational scope.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed nonexclusive six-month capacity-reservation and data-processing agreements specifying panels, volumes, turnaround, cancellation, and roles
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Approach other licensed laboratories, narrow the initial panel, or operate as clinic-paid workflow software without reserved capacity
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each licensed laboratory owns and controls its capacity, methods, results, and clinical obligations
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Clinic retains the patient relationship; founder company owns its B2B clinic and laboratory contracts
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No laboratory, clinic, patient, or health-data access is currently held. The only path is ordinary open-market contracting with licensed entities and explicit, role-appropriate data authorization.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Founder company only after at least two laboratories and one clinic sign compliant agreements
critical_control_point.renewal: Mutual six-month renewal after quality review
critical_control_point.subject: Named panel-processing slots, service levels, and wholesale schedules from multiple licensed laboratories

economics.acquisition_route: Direct clinic contracting and nonexclusive licensed-lab business-development agreements
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not forecast: 200000 annual panels at 60 PLN net platform revenue plus subscriptions imply a low-eight-figure PLN revenue surface; a 5m PLN founder outcome requires regulatory clarity and scalable partner operations
economics.founder_time: Maximum five hours daily only with strict B2B scope and partner-owned clinical support; otherwise defer
economics.gross_margin_basis: Workflow subscription plus spread or take rate after lab, collection, payment, and support costs
economics.payback: Target under six months of account gross profit; long regulated sales cycles may exceed it
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 500-1500 PLN monthly per clinic plus a 5-10% contractually permitted fulfillment fee
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring with every longitudinal panel if turnaround, rejection rate, and reconciliation improve

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Turnaround, rejection, availability, and panel-mapping data improve routing reliability without pooling identifiable health results
fingerprint.customer: Private preventive-medicine clinics and corporate health providers ordering repeat laboratory panels
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct clinic contracting and nonexclusive supply agreements with licensed laboratories and collection networks
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-lab availability, panel mapping, consented order routing, status tracking, and invoice reconciliation without performing or interpreting tests
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Clinic pays a workflow fee or laboratory pays a contracted take rate when an authorized test order is fulfilled
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A clinic needs a defined panel, collection geography, turnaround time, and result interface but negotiates and operates across separate laboratories

founder_fit: Routing and service-level analytics match data-science and operations interests
Neuroscience background supports domain literacy without implying clinical qualification
Orders, turnaround, rejections, and unit contribution are measurable
Software coordination can be part-time only if laboratories and clinics own patient-facing clinical work
risks: A routing or identity error could harm a patient
Merchant-of-record structure may create clinical or tax obligations
Support demands could violate the founder's part-time constraint

structure.commercial_archetype: B2B marketplace and workflow layer over contracted laboratory capacity
structure.control_point: Reserved test-processing and collection capacity under multi-lab agreements
structure.critical_dependency: Licensed laboratories willing to supply capacity, pricing, and compliant interfaces

thesis: Reserve replaceable processing slots and transparent wholesale schedules from multiple licensed medical laboratories, then route standardized clinic-ordered biomarker panels for a platform fee while laboratories retain testing and clinical accountability.
title: Clinic-to-Lab Biomarker Capacity Router
uncertainties: Whether laboratories have contractible spare capacity at attractive wholesale rates
Which party may legally place and route each order
Whether clinics will avoid a single-chain contract for multi-lab resilience
Data-controller and processor roles across clinic, platform, laboratory, and collection point
